reports.name: Miguel Vargas
reports.published_report: Miguel Vargas generates elite contact quality—his 97th percentile xwOBA and 96th percentile xSLG reveal a hitter who makes hard, frequent contact and consistently barrels the ball (14.3% barrel rate, 89th percentile)—yet his .243 average projection exposes a chasing problem that costs him hits. The power and on-base skills project to anchor 30-homer, 97-run production, but Vargas will remain a frustrating swing-and-miss hitter until he cuts chase rate, and his below-average fielding (36th percentile OAA) limits defensive value at third base. High confidence in the skill profile, even as the undiscipline caps his practical ceiling.

reports.published_report: Jurrangelo Cijntje is a high-strikeout arm whose walk rate is dragging down his efficiency—he's at 11.0 K/9 (70th percentile) but 4.9 BB/9 (41st percentile), leaving his K-BB% at just 15% despite solid miss stuff. Over 65.7 innings at AA, a 5.1 ERA and 1.4 WHIP reflect that command gap more than a ceiling problem; the MLB-equivalent translation suggests he'd sit around 4.5 BB/9 at the big-league level, still elevated for a back-end starter profile. Command grade projects at 35, well below the miss grade of 60, making control development the critical fork in the road between useful depth arm and reliable rotation contributor. The sample is fresh and substantial, and ValuCast is moving him up in the rankings, suggesting optimism that he'll tighten the zone.

ValuCast ranks him at organizational depth with a 56% probability of settling into a reserve/depth role, and the recent ranking movement suggests cooling in the projection relative to the current minor-league line.
